title: Development of MEMS Based In-situ TEM Chips and Applications
content: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) has emerged as a pivotal analytical tool in interdisciplinary research spanning chemical synthesis, energy materials development, and structural biology investigations [1,2]. High-resolution imaging and component analysis through TEM can visually present the morphology, structure and chemical composition of the material at atomic scale, which is important for material synthesis, bio-macromolecule analysis and the development of new functional materials. The evolution of TEM technology has facilitated a paradigm shift from static single-frame imaging to real-time dynamic observation. MEMS (Micro Electro Mechanical System) based in-situ chips with varieties of micro components on a single chip, enabled the observation of the dynamic of sample under stimulation of multi-fields (electric, thermal, force, fluid, etc.) in gas or liquid atmosphere [3-5]. We explored the fabrication processes of in-situ chips, and several kinds of high resolution liquid cell chips and high temperature heating chips were developed, including liquid phase flow cell, electrochemical liquid cell, high temperature heating chip (Figure.1). Chip-Nova Technology Co., Ltd helped with the development of high accuracy control system and the program, such as high high-precision temperature control system, which can reach the accuracy of 0.01°C. By bridging static characterization with real-time multimodal analysis, these tools illuminate fundamental mechanisms in chemical synthesis, energy material degradation, and biomolecular interactions, directly informing the design of advanced functional materials.
